Israel Faces Prolonged Political Stalemate as Election Results Show No Clear Winner

29 Oct 2026, 06:35 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.nytimes.com

Key takeaways Election Results Point to No Outright Majority Initial results from Israel’s closely watched election indicate no clear winner, leaving the country facing weeks or months of complex political negotiations. With approximately 90 percent of ballots counted by Wednesday

Election Results Point to No Outright Majority

Initial results from Israel’s closely watched election indicate no clear winner, leaving the country facing weeks or months of complex political negotiations. With approximately 90 percent of ballots counted by Wednesday evening, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s hard-line bloc of parties held a modest lead over the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot. However, neither coalition is projected to win the 61 seats required for a straightforward majority in the 120-seat Knesset, Israel’s Parliament.

Because neither major bloc secured an outright majority, both leaders will need to look outside their traditional coalitions to assemble a governing government. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Netanyahu remains in office as caretaker prime minister while the protracted process plays out.

The Role of Arab Parties and High Turnout

A notable development in the election was a surge in turnout among Arab citizens, who represent about 20 percent of Israel's population. Two predominantly Arab political entities—Raam and the Joint List alliance—are on track to win as many as 19 combined seats, a historically strong showing that positions them as potential kingmakers in the legislative math.

Despite this influence, partnering with Arab factions remains politically difficult for many Jewish parties. Mr. Eisenkot stated that he aims to form a government that is both Zionist and committed to universal military conscription, effectively ruling out alliances with both Arab and ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties. Concurrently, Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud party made unproven allegations regarding the integrity of the vote in Arab communities, claims that were contradicted by official election authorities reporting no widespread irregularities.

Next Steps and Potential Parliamentary Scenarios

The final tally of regular votes is expected to conclude around Thursday evening, though a separate count of over 400,000 special ballots—cast at military bases, hospitals, and prisons—remains ongoing. If political leaders fail to form a governing majority through negotiations, Israel could face the prospect of a repeat election.

Even if a new government is not immediately formed, the newly elected Knesset is scheduled to open on November 10. Opposition lawmakers could potentially leverage a united front in Parliament to take control of the legislative agenda, select a new speaker, and challenge contentious policies or push for independent inquiries.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

  • Caretaker Government: Prime Minister Netanyahu remains in power as caretaker leader until a coalition is successfully formed or alternative electoral steps are taken.
  • Verification: Readers can verify official updates and final vote counts directly through the official coverage provided by [The New York Times Live Updates](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/10/28/world/israel-elections).
  • Confirmed vs. Unknown: It is confirmed that neither major bloc reached the 61-seat threshold based on 90 percent of counted ballots, and that final certified numbers remain pending. It remains entirely unknown how coalition negotiations will unfold or whether the country will be forced into another round of elections.
